content:
“Daily Show” correspondent Michael Kosta sharply criticized President Donald Trump’s seemingly indifferent response to the numerous disruptions to major online systems, including the Federal Aviation Administration, Microsoft, the National Security Agency and Chase Bank.

Speaking to reporters in the Philippines on Tuesday, Trump brushed off questions about whether he was concerned about the outages.

“No. It’s life. It’s life,” Trump said.

“It’s life?” Kosta said. “He’s been in Asia half a day; he’s talking like a fortune cookie.”

“When you’re big and powerful, and you have all the money. Things like that happen. It’s fine,” Trump continued.

Kosta added that it’s easy for Trump to say that because he “doesn’t fly commercial. He doesn’t know how to use email. His bank is a guy from Qatar.”

“For the rest of us, though, it’s not fine,” Kosta said. “So your message to the American people is that things like this happen? I mean, do they?”

Kosta concluded the section of his opening segment with a bizarre but fitting segue, by saying at least the country wasn’t turning into a “massive geyser of rotting garbage.”

Kosta then showed a news clip of a literal massive geyser of rotting garbage that exploded in Los Angeles.
